name: Brighter colours are more pleasant and less dominant

direction.note: The Munsell range is the usual chip range, not a value from the paper.

claim: Colour brightness predicted pleasure strongly and arousal and dominance in the opposite direction, more than hue did.
caveat: Colour chips, not rooms; the weights (pleasure .69, arousal -.31, dominance -.76) come from a quoted abstract and need a check against the paper.

sources.title: Valdez and Mehrabian 1994, Effects of color on emotions, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 123(4)
